Commentary.Commentary: Now Australia would look to redeem themselves with the bat. They have made a couple of changes to their team and will hope that it pays off. Stay tuned as we begin with second innings in a short while.

What a comeback it was by Sri Lanka! Centuries from Dhananjaya de Silva and Dinesh Chandimal did the revival job and took them to a strong position. Starc again proved lethal to the home side as he picked his 7th fifer. Herath had to depart unfortunately after getting hurt off Hazlewood's delivery. Surprisingly, Australia were poor in the field with their skipper dropping two decent chances.

Yet another 5-wicket haul for Mitchell Starc, his 7th in Tests. Superb bowling by the pacer, he's on a roll. His last three innings - 5/63, 6/50, 5/44. SRI LANKA FINISH ON 355!

Dinesh Chandimal, however, kept one end tightly and reached his first Test century against Australia. Soon after that he offered a chance to the visiting team but Steven Smith failed to grab the catch at first slip. Sri Lanka are just one run short of the 300-run mark and given the way the pitch is behaving, if they manage to add another 50 runs to their total, it will test the Aussies. Do join us in a short while to find out how the afternoon session pans out...

Another good session of Test cricket! Sri Lanka scored 85 runs in it while Australia managed to pick up a couple of wickets. The hero of Day 1, Dhananjaya de Silva, didn't add much to his overnight score and fell to Lyon, while Dilruwan Perera in an attempt to score quick runs departed cheaply.

HUNDRED FOR CHANDIMAL! He straightaway jumps in joy and raises his arms in celebration. Wonderful batting. He has been patient and has helped Sri Lanka recover from a precarious situation. Flighted on off, Chandimal nudges it off his pads to square leg for a run. Plenty of emotions shown by the Sri Lankan wicketkeeper batsman and it shows this century means a lot to him. He has batted for over six hours and this has been an extraordinary effort from him. Take a bow, young man!

Russel Arnold says that it is nothing different from Day 1, the cracks are evident as usual but the ball hasn't misbehaved yet. There will be a lot of activity near the footmarks of the bowlers. 73 runs were scored in the last session. Dhananjaya de Silva got to his maiden Test century. The young lad made a statement with this unbeaten knock. He was well supported by his vice captain who is still out there with him on 64. The Aussie bowlers faded away in the end but when they were about to make some breakthroughs, their fielders didn't give them the support at crucial times which frustrated them, and that reflected it in their bowling.

TOSS - Sri Lanka win the toss and elect to bat. They bring in Suranga Lakmal in place of Vishwa Fernando. Australia on the other hand have made a couple of changes, Moises Henriques and Shaun Marsh replace Usman Khawaja and Joe Burns.

Russel Arnold starts with saying that the players will feel the heat as the weather is very hot compared to the earlier venues. The pitch is very dry and the cracks are already evident plus the sun shining over the shoulders will widen the cracks. Seamers will be in the game if they bowl wicket to wicket but moreover, it will favour the spinners. Ends up saying that it will all come down to the batsmen's approach of playing spin and the team will have the upper hand in the match if they score around 275-300.

A warm welcome to everyone! It's the start of the third and final Test of Australia's tour to Sri Lanka which awaits us. It is going to be an excellent day for cricket as the current number one Test side is down under and will look to bounce back to save themselves from the embarrassment of a whitewash. Sri Lanka on the other hand would look to dominate again to gain the bragging rights. Stay tuned as the match will begin in a while.
